content:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a spike in GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast-1 since ~02:10 UTC. A lot of small training jobs getting preempted repeatedly.
jon: saw that too. p95 inference latency up ~40% for the ml-prod route. Any correlating node events?
tara: digging through node events now. quick snippet:
```
$ kubectl describe node gpu-rack-12-node-3
Taints: gpu.dedicated=true:NoSchedule
Events:
  Warning  Eviction  2m  kubelet  Pod //ml-prod-job evicted: node pressure: memory
  Normal   NodeNotReady  1m  kubelet  Node has reported NIC errors
```
lee: NIC errors on the rack, yes — netdev reports spikes, TX drops and queue_full on eth2. We suspect a bad NIC driver causing slow egress -> eviction cascade when kubelet thinks node is degraded.
maria: that matches the autoscaler history — scaled down a rack yesterday night, then warmpool reclaimed and we started packing tiny pods across remaining racks -> increased fragmentation. When one rack shows NIC flapping, the scheduler rebalances and we get mass evictions.
jon: so two compounding issues: (1) taints/tolerations allowing mixed tenant packing (non-dedicated jobs landing on dedicated nodes), (2) network flaps causing nodes to look unhealthy and trigger evictions. Any quick mitigations?
tara: short-term: cordon gpu-rack-12-node-3 and set --eviction-hard to a higher threshold on that kubelet? But that feels risky.
lee: immediate action I can do: cordon the whole rack and move critical inference pods to other AZ if capacity exists. Also open a ticket with NIC vendor.
ops-bot: Incident created: INFRA-1327 — "ap-southeast-1 GPU eviction surge due to rack NIC faults + binpack fragmentation". Pager notified SRE rotation.
sre-jen: For scheduler config: recommend a quick policy tweak — prefer binpack by owner label (tenant=) not absolute, and add a soft taint on dedicated-GPU nodes: gpu.dedicated=true:PreferNoSchedule. That reduces cross-tenant spillover while still permitting emergency placement.
maria: good. Also we should increase kubelet eviction grace for gpu pods to avoid immediate churn and let KV cache warmup finish. Probe: add 30s to terminationGracePeriod for training jobs.
jon: cost note: current churn is adding ~3-4 hours of extra GPU time across clusters (restarts + retries). Rough estimate ~USD 2.3k over the last 12h if not mitigated — we should capture exact billing once INFRA-1327 has EV timeline.
tara: action items: 1) lee cordon rack, 2) ops run node drain for low-priority pods with --delete-emptydir-data, 3) infra change: spin up temp warmpool in ap-southeast-1 (2 nodes) to reduce tight binpack, 4) sched change to PreferNoSchedule + owner-aware binpack rollout behind a flag.
lee: doing step 1 now. will paste commands shortly.
lee: command run:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-rack-12-node-3
kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-rack-12-node-3
kubectl drain gpu-rack-12-node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
```
maria: nice. keep an eye on pending pods — if backpressure goes to control-plane we should throttle new job submissions and enable fallback to cpu-only preview nodes for non-critical tests.
jon: I'll gate the ml-prod job queue for 15m and notify product. @tara can you attach the pod eviction logs to INFRA-1327? we need the event timelines and which pods had tolerations that shouldn't.
tara: yes attaching logs + kubectl get events output. Also I'll list pods without tenant labels — we have a handful that slipped through CI.
sre-jen: long-term proposals (put in INFRA-1327):
- enforce tenant label on GPU PodAdmission webhook
- soft taints for reserved GPU node classes
- scheduler preemption budget per tenant
- rack-aware NIC health probes feeding into placement decisions
- reconcile warmpool sizes dynamically based on p99 pack pressure
maria: all solid. pls update the ticket after the cordon/drain finishes.
lee: cordon + drain completed for node-3. rack still under monitoring. NIC vendor engaged.
ops-bot: Pager status: acknowledged by oncall (sre-jen). Estimated remediation ETA: 45m. Logs attached to INFRA-1327.
jon: thanks team — will post a short customer-facing note if latency doesn't recover in 30m. :thumbsup:
